issue.body:
### What happened?

I'm using `tensor.pad` to pad out some unaligned ops for transpose on the GPU. This results in a cast from the memref type containing the memory space to tensor then back to memref without memory space: 

```mlir
%alloc = memref.alloc() : memref<32x32xf32, 3>
    %10 = bufferization.to_tensor %alloc : memref<32x32xf32, 3>
    %11 = bufferization.to_memref %10 : memref<32x32xf32>
    %c0_3 = arith.constant 0 : index
    %c1 = arith.constant 1 : index
    %c32_4 = arith.constant 32 : index
    %c32_5 = arith.constant 32 : index
    scf.parallel (%arg0, %arg1) = (%c0_3, %c0_3) to (%c32_4, %c32_5) step (%c1, %c1) {
      memref.store %cst, %11[%arg0, %arg1] : memref<32x32xf32>
      scf.yield
    }
    %12 = bufferization.to_tensor %11 : memref<32x32xf32>
    %c1_6 = arith.constant 1 : index
    %dim = memref.dim %subview_0, %c1_6 : memref<32x?xf32, strided<[48, 1], offset: ?>>
    %subview_7 = memref.subview %11[%c0, %c0] [32, %dim] [1, 1] : memref<32x32xf32> to memref<32x?xf32, strided<[32, 1], offset: ?>>
    linalg.generic {indexing_maps = [affine_map<(d0, d1) -> (d0, d1)>, affine_map<(d0, d1) -> (d0, d1)>], iterator_types = ["parallel", "parallel"]} ins(%subview_0 : memref<32x?xf32, strided<[48, 1], offset: ?>>) outs(%subview_7 : memref<32x?xf32, strided<[32, 1], offset: ?>>) {
    ^bb0(%in: f32, %out: f32):
      linalg.yield %in : f32
    }
```

As this IR is lowered further, tensor ops persist after bufferization. This causes failure in compilation due to `unrealized_conversion_cast` operations going into LLVM. See IR here:
https://gist.github.com/KoolJBlack/8a1a13f8de06b6362e9c66e5b01aeb86

and failed test cases here:
https://github.com/iree-org/iree/actions/runs/3252493784/jobs/5338768162

### Steps to reproduce your issue

Note: is the initial IR:
```mlir
func.func @transpose_no_align(%ins: tensor<32x48xf32>) -> tensor<48x32xf32> {
 %0 = "mhlo.transpose"(%ins) {permutation = dense<[1,0]> : tensor<2xi64>} : (tensor<32x48xf32>) -> tensor<48x32xf32>
 return %0 : tensor<48x32xf32>
}
```

To reproduce, issue directly, use this input IR for bufferization. This is the resulting IR from padding out incomplete workgroups to a fixed size of 32x32:

```mlir
func.func @transpose_no_align_dispatch_0_generic_48x32() {
  %c8 = arith.constant 8 : index
  %c32 = arith.constant 32 : index
  %c0 = arith.constant 0 : index
  %cst = arith.constant 0.000000e+00 : f32
  %0 = hal.interface.binding.subspan set(0) binding(0) type(storage_buffer) offset(%c0) alignment(64) : !flow.dispatch.tensor<readonly:32x48xf32>
  %1 = hal.interface.binding.subspan set(0) binding(1) type(storage_buffer) offset(%c0) alignment(64) : !flow.dispatch.tensor<writeonly:48x32xf32>
  %workgroup_id_x = hal.interface.workgroup.id[0] : index
  %workgroup_id_y = hal.interface.workgroup.id[1] : index
  %2 = affine.apply affine_map<()[s0] -> (s0 * 32)>()[%workgroup_id_y]
  %3 = affine.min affine_map<()[s0] -> (s0 * -32 + 48, 32)>()[%workgroup_id_y]
  %4 = affine.apply affine_map<()[s0] -> (s0 * 32)>()[%workgroup_id_x]
  %5 = flow.dispatch.tensor.load %1, offsets = [%2, %4], sizes = [%3, 32], strides = [1, 1] : !flow.dispatch.tensor<writeonly:48x32xf32> -> tensor<?x32xf32>
  %6 = flow.dispatch.tensor.load %0, offsets = [%4, %2], sizes = [32, %3], strides = [1, 1] : !flow.dispatch.tensor<readonly:32x48xf32> -> tensor<32x?xf32>
  %7 = affine.apply affine_map<()[s0] -> (-s0 + 32)>()[%3]
  %padded = tensor.pad %6 low[%c0, %c0] high[%c0, %7] {
  ^bb0(%arg0: index, %arg1: index):
    tensor.yield %cst : f32
  } : tensor<32x?xf32> to tensor<32x32xf32>
  %padded_0 = tensor.pad %5 low[%c0, %c0] high[%7, %c0] {
  ^bb0(%arg0: index, %arg1: index):
    tensor.yield %cst : f32
  } : tensor<?x32xf32> to tensor<32x32xf32>
  %8 = scf.foreach_thread (%arg0, %arg1) in (%c32, %c8) shared_outs(%arg2 = %padded_0) -> (tensor<32x32xf32>) {
    %9 = affine.apply affine_map<(d0) -> (d0 * 4)>(%arg1)
    %extracted_slice_1 = tensor.extract_slice %arg2[%arg0, %9] [1, 4] [1, 1] : tensor<32x32xf32> to tensor<1x4xf32>
    %10 = vector.transfer_read %padded[%9, %arg0], %cst {in_bounds = [true, true]} : tensor<32x32xf32>, vector<4x1xf32>
    %11 = vector.shape_cast %10 : vector<4x1xf32> to vector<1x4xf32>
    %12 = vector.extract %11[0] : vector<1x4xf32>
    %13 = vector.transfer_write %12, %extracted_slice_1[%c0, %c0] {in_bounds = [true]} : vector<4xf32>, tensor<1x4xf32>
    scf.foreach_thread.perform_concurrently {
      tensor.parallel_insert_slice %13 into %arg2[%arg0, %9] [1, 4] [1, 1] : tensor<1x4xf32> into tensor<32x32xf32>
    }
  } {thread_dim_mapping = [1, 0, 2]}
  %extracted_slice = tensor.extract_slice %8[0, 0] [%3, 32] [1, 1] : tensor<32x32xf32> to tensor<?x32xf32>
  flow.dispatch.tensor.store %extracted_slice, %1, offsets = [%2, %4], sizes = [%3, 32], strides = [1, 1] : tensor<?x32xf32> -> !flow.dispatch.tensor<writeonly:48x32xf32>
  return
}

```

Run bufferization with IREE-OPT:

```
tools/iree-opt \
-iree-codegen-iree-comprehensive-bufferize \
input/bufferize-input.mlir \
output/bufferize-output.mlir \
```


### What component(s) does this issue relate to?

Compiler

### Version information

https://github.com/iree-org/iree/commit/b416bf7d4cfd428b3b455a4ae62102bbe2d29263

### Additional context

Related to https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/10005

Discovered in https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/10731

issue.title: Tensor::PadOp bufferization doesn't support CUDA Shared Memory Space 3

issue.body:
This removes specialization from the transpose pipeline as it is redundant since padding handles non-alignment. 

Updated TensorAllocPass to account for padded tensors during transpose. These are skipped during allocation. 

Note: Transpose padding is currently not distributed, hence the inclusion of `linalg.generic` in the padded test output. 

Part of https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/10005
